sanskrit: bhāgyaṃ nakṣatram ākramya sūryaputreṇa pīḍyate śukraḥ proṣṭhapade pūrve samāruhya viśāṃ pate uttare tu parikramya sahitaḥ pratyudīkṣate
english: Encroaching upon the lunar mansion Bhāgya, Śukra is afflicted by the son of Sūrya; having mounted into the eastern Proṣṭhapada, O lord of peoples, and then circled round into the northern, he stands waiting in conjunction.

sanskrit: śyāmo grahaḥ prajvalitaḥ sadhūmaḥ sahapāvakaḥ aindraṃ tejasvi nakṣatraṃ jyeṣṭhām ākramya tiṣṭhati
english: A dark planet, blazing, wreathed in smoke and fire, has encroached upon the brilliant mansion of Indra, Jyeṣṭhā, and there it stands.

sanskrit: dhruvaḥ prajvalito ghoram apasavyaṃ pravartate citrāsvātyantare caiva dhiṣṭhitaḥ paruṣo grahaḥ
english: The Pole Star, blazing dreadfully, turns from right to left; and a harsh planet has taken its station between Citrā and Svāti.

sanskrit: vakrānuvakraṃ kṛtvā ca śravaṇe pāvakaprabhaḥ brahmarāśiṃ samāvṛtya lohitāṅgo vyavasthitaḥ
english: Moving in retrograde and counter-retrograde course, bright as fire upon Śravaṇa, the Red-bodied one (Mars) has overspread the constellation of Brahmā and there abides.

sanskrit: sarvasasyapraticchannā pṛthivī phalamālinī pañcaśīrṣā yavāś caiva śataśīrṣāś ca śālayaḥ
english: The earth, mantled with every kind of grain and garlanded with fruit, brings forth barley with five heads and rice with a hundred heads.

sanskrit: pradhānāḥ sarvalokasya yāsv āyattam idaṃ jagat tā gāvaḥ prasnutā vatsaiḥ śoṇitaṃ prakṣaranty uta
english: The cows, foremost of all the world, upon whom this whole creation depends — they, giving milk to their calves, ooze blood instead.

sanskrit: niścerur apidhānebhyaḥ khaḍgāḥ prajvalitā bhṛśam vyaktaṃ paśyanti śastrāṇi saṃgrāmaṃ samupasthitam
english: Swords, fiercely ablaze, leap forth from their scabbards; plainly the weapons foresee the battle now at hand.

sanskrit: agnivarṇā yathā bhāsaḥ śastrāṇām udakasya ca kavacānāṃ dhvajānāṃ ca bhaviṣyati mahān kṣayaḥ
english: The radiance of the weapons and of the waters is as the color of fire; there shall be a great destruction of armor and of banners.

sanskrit: dikṣu prajvalitāsyāś ca vyāharanti mṛgadvijāḥ atyāhitaṃ darśayanto vedayanti mahad bhayam
english: Toward the quarters of the sky, beasts and birds with flaming mouths cry out, foretelling calamity and announcing a great terror.

sanskrit: ekapakṣākṣicaraṇaḥ śakuniḥ khacaro niśi raudraṃ vadati saṃrabdhaḥ śoṇitaṃ chardayan muhuḥ
english: A bird with but one wing, one eye, and one foot, ranging the sky by night, cries out fiercely in its rage, spewing forth blood again and again.

sanskrit: grahau tāmrāruṇaśikhau prajvalantāv iva sthitau saptarṣīṇām udārāṇāṃ samavacchādya vai prabhām
english: Two planets, copper-red of crest and seeming to blaze, stand there, having veiled over the splendor of the noble Seven Seers.

sanskrit: saṃvatsarasthāyinau ca grahau prajvalitāv ubhau viśākhayoḥ samīpasthau bṛhaspatiśanaiścarau
english: And both planets, abiding for a full year and both ablaze — Bṛhaspati and Śanaiścara (Jupiter and Saturn) — stand close beside the two stars of Viśākhā.

sanskrit: kṛttikāsu grahas tīvro nakṣatre prathame jvalan vapūṃṣy apaharan bhāsā dhūmaketur iva sthitaḥ
english: In Kṛttikā, the first of mansions, a fierce planet, blazing and stealing away forms with its glare, stands like a smoking comet.

sanskrit: triṣu pūrveṣu sarveṣu nakṣatreṣu viśāṃ pate budhaḥ saṃpatate 'bhīkṣṇaṃ janayan sumahad bhayam
english: Through all three of the earlier mansions, O lord of peoples, Budha (Mercury) repeatedly speeds, engendering exceedingly great fear.

sanskrit: caturdaśīṃ pañcadaśīṃ bhūtapūrvāṃ ca ṣoḍaśīm imāṃ tu nābhijānāmi amāvāsyāṃ trayodaśīm
english: A fourteenth-day moon, a fifteenth-day moon, and once even a sixteenth I have known; but this new moon falling on a thirteenth day I have never known before.

sanskrit: candrasūryāv ubhau grastāv ekamāse trayodaśīm aparvaṇi grahāv etau prajāḥ saṃkṣapayiṣyataḥ
english: Both moon and sun eclipsed within a single month, on the thirteenth day and out of their proper season — these two seizures shall bring the peoples to ruin.

sanskrit: rajovṛtā diśaḥ sarvāḥ pāṃsuvarṣaiḥ samantataḥ utpātameghā raudrāś ca rātrau varṣanti śoṇitam
english: All the quarters are wrapped in dust, with showers of grit on every side; and dreadful portent-clouds rain down blood in the night.

sanskrit: māṃsavarṣaṃ punas tīvram āsīt kṛṣṇacaturdaśīm ardharātre mahāghoram atṛpyaṃs tatra rākṣasāḥ
english: Again, on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight, at midnight, there came a fierce and most terrible rain of flesh, whereat the rākṣasas glutted themselves unsated.

sanskrit: pratisroto 'vahan nadyaḥ saritaḥ śoṇitodakāḥ phenāyamānāḥ kūpāś ca nardanti vṛṣabhā iva patanty ulkāḥ sanirghātāḥ śuṣkāśanivimiśritāḥ
english: The rivers flowed backward against their stream, their waters turned to blood; the wells, foaming over, bellow like bulls; and meteors fall amid thunderclaps, mingled with dry lightning-bolts.

sanskrit: adya caiva niśāṃ vyuṣṭām udaye bhānur āhataḥ jvalantībhir maholkābhiś caturbhiḥ sarvatodiśam
english: And this very day, when the night had passed, at sunrise the sun was struck on every side by four great blazing meteors.

sanskrit: ādityam upatiṣṭhadbhis tatra coktaṃ maharṣibhiḥ bhūmipālasahasrāṇāṃ bhūmiḥ pāsyati śoṇitam
english: And the great seers, as they paid worship to the Sun, declared therein: the earth shall drink the blood of thousands of kings.

sanskrit: kailāsamandarābhyāṃ tu tathā himavato gireḥ sahasraśo mahāśabdaṃ śikharāṇi patanti ca
english: From Kailāsa and Mandara, and from the mountain Himavat as well, peaks crash down by the thousand with a mighty roar.

sanskrit: mahābhūtā bhūmikampe caturaḥ sāgarān pṛthak velām udvartayanti sma kṣobhayantaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: In the quaking of the earth the great elemental beings make each of the four oceans, severally, heave up their shores, churning them again and again.

sanskrit: vṛkṣān unmathya vānty ugrā vātāḥ śarkarakarṣiṇaḥ patanti caityavṛkṣāś ca grāmeṣu nagareṣu ca
english: Fierce winds blow, uprooting trees and dragging gravel along; and the sacred shrine-trees topple down in villages and in cities.

sanskrit: pītalohitanīlaś ca jvalaty agnir huto dvijaiḥ vāmārciḥ śāvagandhī ca dhūmaprāyaḥ kharasvanaḥ sparśā gandhā rasāś caiva viparītā mahīpate
english: The fire, when offered into by the brāhmaṇas, blazes up yellow, red, and blue, its flame veering leftward, smelling of corpses, thick with smoke and harsh of sound; and touch, smell, and taste are all turned awry, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: dhūmāyante dhvajā rājñāṃ kampamānā muhur muhuḥ muñcanty aṅgāravarṣāṇi bheryo 'tha paṭahās tathā
english: The banners of the kings smoke and quiver again and again, and shed showers of live coals; and so too do the kettledrums and the war-drums.

sanskrit: prāsādaśikharāgreṣu puradvāreṣu caiva hi gṛdhrāḥ paripatanty ugrā vāmaṃ maṇḍalam āśritāḥ
english: Upon the tops of palace-spires and at the city gates fierce vultures wheel and settle, taking up a circling course to the left.

sanskrit: pakvāpakveti subhṛśaṃ vāvāśyante vayāṃsi ca nilīyante dhvajāgreṣu kṣayāya pṛthivīkṣitām
english: And the birds cry out shrilly, again and again, "Cooked! cooked!" and roost upon the banner-tips, portending the destruction of the rulers of the earth.

sanskrit: dhyāyantaḥ prakirantaś ca vālān vepathusaṃyutāḥ rudanti dīnās turagā mātaṅgāś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: Brooding and shaking out their tails, trembling all over, the horses and the elephants, piteous, weep by the thousand.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā bhavān atra prāptakālaṃ vyavasyatām yathā lokaḥ samucchedaṃ nāyaṃ gaccheta bhārata
english: Having heard all this, let your lordship resolve upon what the hour demands, so that this world may not go to utter ruin, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pitur vaco niśamyaitad dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bravīd idam diṣṭam etat purā manye bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard these words of his father, Dhṛtarāṣṭra spoke thus: This, I think, was ordained long ago; it shall come to pass, there is no doubt.

sanskrit: kṣatriyāḥ kṣatradharmeṇa vadhyante yadi saṃyuge vīralokaṃ samāsādya sukhaṃ prāpsyanti kevalam
english: If kṣatriyas are slain in battle according to the law of kṣatriyas, then, attaining the world of heroes, they shall win nothing but bliss.

sanskrit: iha kīrtiṃ pare loke dīrghakālaṃ mahat sukham prāpsyanti puruṣavyāghrāḥ prāṇāṃs tyaktvā mahāhave
english: These tigers among men, having yielded up their lives in the great battle, shall win renown here and, in the world beyond, great happiness for a long age.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam ukto munis tattvaṃ kavīndro rājasattama putreṇa dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa dhyānam anvagamat param
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by his son Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the sage, lord of poets, O best of kings, knowing the truth of things, sank into deep meditation.

sanskrit: punar evābravīd vākyaṃ kālavādī mahātapāḥ asaṃśayaṃ pārthivendra kālaḥ saṃkṣipate jagat
english: Then once more the great ascetic, the proclaimer of Time, spoke these words: Without doubt, O lord of kings, it is Time that draws the world together to its end.

sanskrit: sṛjate ca punar lokān neha vidyati śāśvatam jñātīnāṃ ca kurūṇāṃ ca saṃbandhisuhṛdāṃ tathā
english: And again Time brings forth the worlds; nothing here is everlasting — neither of your kinsmen, nor of the Kurus, nor of your allies and friends.

sanskrit: dharmyaṃ deśaya panthānaṃ samartho hy asi vāraṇe kṣudraṃ jñātivadhaṃ prāhur mā kuruṣva mamāpriyam
english: Point out the righteous path, for you are able to hold them back; men call the slaughter of one's own kin a base thing — do not do what is hateful to me.

sanskrit: kālo 'yaṃ putrarūpeṇa tava jāto viśāṃ pate na vadhaḥ pūjyate vede hitaṃ naitat kathaṃ cana
english: This is Time, born in the shape of your son, O lord of peoples. In the Veda no slaughter is honored; this is in no wise a good.

sanskrit: hanyāt sa eva yo hanyāt kuladharmaṃ svakāṃ tanum kālenotpathagantāsi śakye sati yathāpathi
english: He who would slay his own kindred slays the law of his line and his very own body. By the power of Time you are about to stray from the path, though, while it is yet possible, you might keep to the road.

sanskrit: kulasyāsya vināśāya tathaiva ca mahīkṣitām anartho rājyarūpeṇa tyajyatām asukhāvahaḥ
english: For the destruction of this house, and likewise of the rulers of the earth, this calamity has come in the guise of kingship — let it be cast off, this bringer of misery.

sanskrit: luptaprajñaḥ pareṇāsi dharmaṃ darśaya vai sutān kiṃ te rājyena durdharṣa yena prāpto 'si kilbiṣam
english: By another your wisdom has been undone; show your sons the path of dharma. What use to you, O unassailable one, is a kingdom by which you have come to sin?

sanskrit: yaśo dharmaṃ ca kīrtiṃ ca pālayan svargam āpsyasi labhantāṃ pāṇḍavā rājyaṃ śamaṃ gacchantu kauravāḥ
english: Guarding your honor, your dharma, and your renown, you shall win heaven. Let the Pāṇḍavas have the kingdom, and let the Kauravas come to peace.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvati viprendre dhṛtarāṣṭro 'mbikāsutaḥ ākṣipya vākyaṃ vākyajño vākpathenāpy ayāt punaḥ
english: As the foremost of brāhmaṇas spoke thus, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Ambikā, skilled in speech, broke in upon his words and went again into the way of discourse.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yathā bhavān veda tathāsmi vettā; bhāvābhāvau viditau me yathāvat svārthe hi saṃmuhyati tāta loko; māṃ cāpi lokātmakam eva viddhi
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Even as your lordship knows, so do I know; being and non-being are known to me as they truly are. Yet in its own concerns, dear sir, the world is bewildered — and know me too to be of one nature with the world.

sanskrit: prasādaye tvām atulaprabhāvaṃ; tvaṃ no gatir darśayitā ca dhīraḥ na cāpi te vaśagā me maharṣe; na kalmaṣaṃ kartum ihārhase mām
english: I beseech you of matchless might: you are our refuge and our steadfast guide. But these of mine are not in my power, O great seer; you ought not to burden me here with the guilt.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi dharmaḥ pavitraṃ ca yaśaḥ kīrtir dhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca mānyaś cāsi pitāmahaḥ
english: For you are dharma itself, and purity, honor, renown, constancy, and memory; and you are the venerable grandsire of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas alike.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca vaicitravīrya nṛpate yat te manasi vartate abhidhatsva yathākāmaṃ chettāsmi tava saṃśayam
english: Vyāsa said: O king, son of Vicitravīrya, whatever stirs within your mind, speak it freely as you will; I shall cut away your doubt.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yāni liṅgāni saṃgrāme bhavanti vijayiṣyatām tāni sarvāṇi bhagavañ śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Those signs which appear in battle for them that shall be victorious — all of these, O blessed one, I wish to hear of truly.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca prasannabhāḥ pāvaka ūrdhvaraśmiḥ; pradakṣiṇāvartaśikho vidhūmaḥ puṇyā gandhāś cāhutīnāṃ pravānti; jayasyaitad bhāvino rūpam āhuḥ
english: Vyāsa said: When the fire is clear of radiance, its beams rising upward, its flame whirling to the right and free of smoke, and holy fragrances waft from the oblations — this, they say, is the very mark of coming victory.

sanskrit: gambhīraghoṣāś ca mahāsvanāś ca; śaṅkhā mṛdaṅgāś ca nadanti yatra viśuddharaśmis tapanaḥ śaśī ca; jayasyaitad bhāvino rūpam āhuḥ
english: Where conches and drums, deep-voiced and loud-sounding, resound, and the sun and the moon shine with rays unsullied — this, they say, is the very mark of coming victory.

sanskrit: iṣṭā vācaḥ pṛṣṭhato vāyasānāṃ; saṃprasthitānāṃ ca gamiṣyatāṃ ca ye pṛṣṭhatas te tvarayanti rājan; ye tv agratas te pratiṣedhayanti
english: Auspicious are the cries of crows behind those who have set out and those about to go, O king: those behind urge them onward, while those in front would hold them back.

sanskrit: kalyāṇavācaḥ śakunā rājahaṃsāḥ; śukāḥ krauñcāḥ śatapatrāś ca yatra pradakṣiṇāś caiva bhavanti saṃkhye; dhruvaṃ jayaṃ tatra vadanti viprāḥ
english: Where birds of fair-sounding voice — royal swans, parrots, herons, and woodpeckers — wheel to the right in the battle, there the brāhmaṇas declare victory is certain.

sanskrit: alaṃkāraiḥ kavacaiḥ ketubhiś ca; mukhaprasādair hemavarṇaiś ca nṝṇām bhrājiṣmatī duṣpratiprekṣaṇīyā; yeṣāṃ camūs te vijayanti śatrūn
english: They whose host is radiant and hard to look upon for its splendor — with ornaments, armor, and standards, and with the golden-hued, serene faces of its men — they conquer their foes.

sanskrit: hṛṣṭā vācas tathā sattvaṃ yodhānāṃ yatra bhārata na mlāyante srajaś caiva te taranti raṇe ripūn
english: Where the voices and the spirit of the warriors are glad, O Bhārata, and their garlands do not wither, they overcome their enemies in battle.

sanskrit: iṣṭo vātaḥ praviṣṭasya dakṣiṇā pravivikṣataḥ paścāt saṃsādhayaty arthaṃ purastāt pratiṣedhate
english: A favorable wind from the south, for one who has entered or is about to enter the field, accomplishes his purpose when at his back, but thwarts it when in his face.

sanskrit: śabdarūparasasparśagandhāś cāviṣkṛtāḥ śubhāḥ sadā yodhāś ca hṛṣṭāś ca yeṣāṃ teṣāṃ dhruvaṃ jayaḥ
english: They for whom sound, form, taste, touch, and smell show themselves auspicious, and whose warriors are ever glad — for them victory is sure.

sanskrit: anv eva vāyavo vānti tathābhrāṇi vayāṃsi ca anuplavante meghāś ca tathaivendradhanūṃṣi ca
english: The winds blow in their favor, and so the clouds and the birds, and the storm-clouds float along behind them, and so too do the rainbows.

sanskrit: etāni jayamānānāṃ lakṣaṇāni viśāṃ pate bhavanti viparītāni mumūrṣūṇāṃ janādhipa
english: These, O lord of peoples, are the marks of them that are winning; for them that are about to die they are reversed, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: alpāyāṃ vā mahatyāṃ vā senāyām iti niścitam harṣo yodhagaṇasyaikaṃ jayalakṣaṇam ucyate
english: Whether the army be small or great, this is held for certain: the gladness of the host of warriors is, by itself, called a mark of victory.

sanskrit: eko dīrṇo dārayati senāṃ sumahatīm api taṃ dīrṇam anudīryante yodhāḥ śūratamā api
english: A single man, broken in spirit, breaks even a very great army; and after that one broken man even the bravest warriors give way in turn.

sanskrit: durnivāratamā caiva prabhagnā mahatī camūḥ apām iva mahāvegas trastā mṛgagaṇā iva
english: And a great host once shattered is most hard to check, like the mighty rush of waters, like a herd of deer struck with panic.

sanskrit: naiva śakyā samādhātuṃ saṃnipāte mahācamūḥ dīrṇā ity eva dīryante yodhāḥ śūratamā api bhītān bhagnāṃś ca saṃprekṣya bhayaṃ bhūyo vivardhate
english: In the clash of battle a great host, once broken, can in no way be set in order again; at the mere word "broken!" even the bravest warriors are broken, and at the sight of men frightened and routed the terror swells the more.

sanskrit: prabhagnā sahasā rājan diśo vibhrāmitā paraiḥ naiva sthāpayituṃ śakyā śūrair api mahācamūḥ
english: A great host suddenly shattered, O king, and driven scattering to the quarters by the foe, cannot be made to stand fast, not even by brave men.

sanskrit: saṃbhṛtya mahatīṃ senāṃ caturaṅgāṃ mahīpatiḥ upāyapūrvaṃ medhāvī yateta satatotthitaḥ
english: Having gathered a great army of the four arms, let the wise king, ever vigilant, strive by means of good policy first of all.

sanskrit: upāyavijayaṃ śreṣṭham āhur bhedena madhyamam jaghanya eṣa vijayo yo yuddhena viśāṃ pate mahādoṣaḥ saṃnipātas tato vyaṅgaḥ sa ucyate
english: Victory by stratagem they call the best, by sowing discord the middling; lowest is that victory which is won by battle, O lord of peoples. The pitched clash is a great evil, and therefore it is called the maimed kind of conquest.

sanskrit: parasparajñāḥ saṃhṛṣṭā vyavadhūtāḥ suniścitāḥ pañcāśad api ye śūrā mathnanti mahatīṃ camūm atha vā pañca ṣaṭ sapta vijayanty anivartinaḥ
english: Brave men who know one another well, full of spirit, resolute and steadfast — even fifty such churn up a mighty host; or even five, six, or seven, who will not turn back, win the day.

sanskrit: na vainateyo garuḍaḥ praśaṃsati mahājanam dṛṣṭvā suparṇopacitiṃ mahatīm api bhārata
english: Garuḍa, son of Vinatā, does not esteem a great multitude, O Bhārata, even on beholding a vast gathering of fine-feathered birds.

sanskrit: na bāhulyena senāyā jayo bhavati bhārata adhruvo hi jayo nāma daivaṃ cātra parāyaṇam jayanto hy api saṃgrāme kṣayavanto bhavanty uta
english: Victory does not come by the mere multitude of an army, O Bhārata; victory, indeed, is a thing uncertain, and fate is here the final refuge; for even those who win in battle suffer their own losses.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā yayau vyāso dhṛtarāṣṭrāya dhīmate dhṛtarāṣṭro 'pi tac chrutvā dhyānam evānvapadyata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus to the wise Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Vyāsa departed; and Dhṛtarāṣṭra too, having heard it, sank into meditation.

sanskrit: sa muhūrtam iva dhyātvā viniḥśvasya muhur muhuḥ saṃjayaṃ saṃśitātmānam apṛcchad bharatarṣabha
english: Having brooded for the space of a moment, and sighing again and again, he questioned Saṃjaya of disciplined soul, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: saṃjayeme mahīpālāḥ śūrā yuddhābhinandinaḥ anyonyam abhinighnanti śastrair uccāvacair api
english: Saṃjaya, these rulers of the earth, heroes who delight in battle, strike one another down with weapons high and low.

sanskrit: pārthivāḥ pṛthivīhetoḥ samabhityaktajīvitāḥ na ca śāmyanti nighnanto vardhayanto yamakṣayam
english: The kings, having flung away their very lives for the earth's sake, do not cease from the slaughter, swelling the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: bhaumam aiśvaryam icchanto na mṛṣyante parasparam manye bahuguṇā bhūmis tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Coveting earthly sovereignty, they cannot endure one another. The earth, I think, must hold many a virtue; tell me of it, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: bahūni ca sahasrāṇi prayutāny arbudāni ca koṭyaś ca lokavīrāṇāṃ sametāḥ kurujāṅgale
english: Many thousands, many myriads, hundreds of millions, and tens of millions of the world's heroes are gathered together in Kurujāṅgala.

sanskrit: deśānāṃ ca parīmāṇaṃ nagarāṇāṃ ca saṃjaya śrotum icchāmi tattvena yata ete samāgatāḥ
english: And the measure of the lands and of the cities from which these have come together, Saṃjaya, I wish to hear of truly.

sanskrit: divyabuddhipradīpena yuktas tvaṃ jñānacakṣuṣā prasādāt tasya viprarṣer vyāsasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: You are endowed with the lamp of divine understanding and with the eye of knowledge, by the grace of that brāhmaṇa-seer Vyāsa of measureless splendor.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yathāprajñaṃ mahāprājña bhaumān vakṣyāmi te guṇān śāstracakṣur avekṣasva namas te bharatarṣabha
english: Saṃjaya said: As far as my understanding reaches, O greatly wise one, I shall tell you of the earth's qualities; look on them with the eye of the scriptures. Homage to you, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: dvividhānīha bhūtāni trasāni sthāvarāṇi ca trasānāṃ trividhā yonir aṇḍasvedajarāyujāḥ
english: Beings here are of two kinds: the moving and the unmoving. Of the moving, the womb is threefold — those born of eggs, of sweat, and of the womb-membrane.

sanskrit: trasānāṃ khalu sarveṣāṃ śreṣṭhā rājañ jarāyujāḥ jarāyujānāṃ pravarā mānavāḥ paśavaś ca ye
english: Of all moving beings, O king, the womb-born are the foremost; and of the womb-born, the highest are humankind and the beasts that there are.

sanskrit: nānārūpāṇi bibhrāṇās teṣāṃ bhedāś caturdaśa araṇyavāsinaḥ sapta saptaiṣāṃ grāmavāsinaḥ
english: Bearing manifold forms, of these there are fourteen divisions: seven that dwell in the wilderness and seven of them that dwell in villages.
